promptInstructions: Draft a petition for Judicial Separation under S.10 HMA (or S.23 SMA, as selected).
Plead valid marriage averments per governing statute (Hindu rites for HMA; SMA certificate for SMA).
Plead cohabitation period and date of cessation of cohabitation.
S.10(1) HMA allows judicial separation on ANY of the grounds specified in S.13(1) (for either spouse) and S.13(2) (for wife). Same body of grounds — pleadings mirror divorce.
Key distinction: A decree of judicial separation does NOT dissolve the marriage. It only relieves parties of the obligation to cohabit. Re-marriage during subsistence is bigamy.
Explain (where relevant) why petitioner seeks separation rather than divorce — religious / personal / reconciliation hope. This strengthens bona fides.
Include S.23(1) averments: no collusion, no condonation, no improper delay, no taking advantage of own wrong.
Plead jurisdiction under S.19 HMA / S.31 SMA.
Note: After 1 year non-resumption of cohabitation following a judicial separation decree, S.13(1A)(i) HMA allows either party to seek divorce.
Tone is restrained — petitioner is preserving the marriage tie while seeking relief from cohabitation.

sections.description: Petition for judicial separation on any ground specified in S.13(1) or, in case of wife, S.13(2)
Where decree of judicial separation passed, parties not obliged to cohabit; court may rescind on application
Non-resumption of cohabitation for 1 year post-judicial separation — independent ground for divorce
Judicial separation under SMA — analogous to S.10 HMA

key_citations: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511 — cruelty principles apply equally for separation
Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash (1991) 2 SCC 25 — withdrawal of consent applies to S.13B; not to S.10
Hirachand Srinivas Managaonkar v. Sunanda (2001) 4 SCC 125 — judicial separation decree-holder seeking divorce under S.13(1A)(i) — disqualification under S.23(1)(a) if 'wrong' continues
